name: Long Wave: Dispatches from the Fringe
creator: Yusuf Achterberg-Nwosu, field journalist
description: A solo documentary broadcast project run by itinerant journalist Yusuf Achterberg-Nwosu, Long Wave transmits irregular long-form field recordings from Meridian's margins — the Iowa border settlements, the flooded lower Shelf, migrant processing corridors, and the gray zones where corponation authority frays into improvised governance. Each episode is a single unedited transmission, often running four to eight hours, combining ambient audio, direct testimony, and Achterberg-Nwosu's own running commentary. The broadcast goes out on whatever channel is available at the time of recording.
medium: neural feed (gray market), legacy audio, physical data chip (retrospective archive)
cultural_impact: Long Wave is the only sustained broadcast record of conditions in the Iowa border settlements and the flooded Shelf sub-levels; its recordings have been entered as evidence in two international human rights proceedings and are archived by three universities outside Meridian's corponation jurisdiction.
controversy: Achterberg-Nwosu was briefly detained by Iowa Autonomous Zone perimeter security in 2219 while attempting to document Behemoth movement patterns from the border settlements; the resulting episode, 'Seventeen Hours at the Wire,' is his most-distributed broadcast and is banned from all licensed neural feed channels.
story_hooks: Achterberg-Nwosu's latest transmission cuts out mid-broadcast from a location near the Iowa perimeter; his last words reference something he's seeing that doesn't match any known Behemoth classification.
A corponation legal team is attempting to have Long Wave's archived episodes classified as 'unauthorized surveillance data' — which would retroactively criminalize everyone who downloaded them.

Achterberg-Nwosu contacts a Shelf community asking to document their situation; the community is divided — some see it as their only chance to be heard, others fear that visibility will make them a target.
